absent: Bio submission, splitting, cloning, chaining, completion and reference-count transitions beyond field roles.
Request-queue remainder past the truncated fragment and elevator, multiqueue ops, tag, timeout and requeue protocols.
Lock ordering among queue lock, requeue lock, QoS mutex, cgroup mutex and zone plug locks.
Cgroup, crypto, integrity and QoS lifecycle and accounting rules.
Partition scanning, disk add and removal, event polling and uevent emission procedures.
Zone plug worker, hash sizing, zone condition updates and zone-append emulation steps.
Flush state machine, stats collection, power-only mode and error-injection behavior.
Block address triple allocation and minor-range management.

findings.text: A block IO descriptor chains to a successor, names a target device, and carries a combined operation word, small flag and priority fields, write lifetime hints, a status value, a DMA gap hint, a remaining counter, a vector base pointer plus iterator, a shared slot used either as poll cookie or segment count, a completion routine plus opaque token, optional cgroup, crypto and integrity links, live and allocated vector counts, a pin count and an owning pool link.

Reset preserves the vector array pointer and everything at and after the allocated-vector-count field. A byte count derived from the offset of that field defines the reset span. Live vector count and allocation size are distinct: allocation size guides submission-time append failure and freeing, while live count describes current membership.
Maximum IO length equals the largest unsigned integer and bounds the iterator size. Maximum sector count is that length shifted down by sector size. These two values cap a single descriptor.

Per-descriptor state bits cover page pinning, cloned data ownership, quiet completion, chaining with remaining accounting, elevated pin count, block throttling once, completion tracing, cgroup accounting, quality-of-service throttling and merging, remapping, zone write plugging, zone append emulation, task-context completion, and a last sentinel. One throttling alias shares the QoS throttling value.
An operation word packs an 8 bit operation in the low part and 24 bits of flags above it. A mask isolates the low operation. A 32 bit bitwise type represents multiqueue request flags.

Operation codes include read 0, write 1, cache flush 2, discard 3, secure erase 5, zone append 7, write zeroes 9, zone open 11, zone close 13, zone finish 15, zone reset 17, reset all zones 19, driver inbound 34, driver outbound 35, and a last marker 36. Unlisted values in gaps have no assigned meaning in the fragment.

Request modifier bits start above the operation field and cover device, transport and driver failfast, synchronous, metadata, priority boost, no merge, idle anticipation, integrity payload, forced access, preflush, readahead, background, no-wait, polled completion, cache allocation, swap, driver private, submitter private, atomic write, and no-unmap for zeroing. One mask combines the three failfast bits; another combines no-merge with preflush and forced access.
A request timing summary holds mean, minimum, maximum, sample count and batch accumulator as integers. Statistics are grouped into read, write, discard and flush buckets with a group count sentinel.

Four small classifiers are provided: one reports flush character when either forced-access or preflush is set; one reports discard by masking then comparing; one reports zone management for reset, reset-all, open, close and finish; one maps an operation to a statistics bucket, sending discard to its bucket and otherwise using the write indicator.

Partition and disk sizing facts: at most 256 partitions, driver name room for 32 bytes, volume name room for 64 bytes, and UUID room for the string form plus terminator. A metadata record pairs a UUID character array with a volume-name byte array.

Whole-disk behavior flags mark removable, hidden, and no-partition devices. Device events distinguish media change from eject request. Event handling flags control polling without an interval, forwarding to userspace, and blocking polls during exclusive-write opens.

Integrity support uses a packed four-valued checksum selector for none, IP style, CRC and 64 bit CRC, plus a descriptor holding flags, selector, metadata size, protection offset, interval exponent, tag size and tuple size.
Block open modes are six distinct single-bit values for read, write, exclusive, no-delay, write-flavored control, restricted writes and strict scanning.

A disk object stores address triple, fixed-size name, supported and active event masks, a partition index plus primary partition link, operation vector, queue link, driver-private word, split pool, integer flags, bit state, open-partition count, backing-device info, queue and slave directory objects, randomness state, event state, optional zoned topology and plugging structures, optional optical-device link, node id, bad-block map, lock tracking, sequence number, current open mode, optional independent-range map, optional error-injection state, and a quality-of-service state mutex.

Disk state bit positions 0 through 8 respectively mean scan needed, read-only, dead, native capacity exposed, added, suppress scanning, owns its queue, zone-append observed, and error injection active.

Disk open and close paths serialize on a dedicated mutex. Quality-of-service state changes use a separate mutex, and error injection has its own mutex when enabled. Zone plug hash and list each have a spin lock with a dedicated pool, hash table, list, worker thread, workqueue and completion. Zone condition reads use RCU with queue-enter and queue-exit protection.

Disk helpers expose opener count from the primary partition, a scan-eligibility test combining no-part and hidden flags with the suppress-scan state, conversions between device, disk and backing-device objects, an optical-device accessor with present and absent build variants, and a device-number constructor from major and first minor.

In-kernel device-number construction shifts the major by a minor-bit count then adds the minor, while the user-visible construction shifts the major by eight then adds the minor. The two encodings differ and must not be interchanged.

Block-size validation accepts only powers of two between 512 and a build-dependent ceiling, returning a negative invalid-argument result otherwise. The ceiling is 64 KiB in one build alternative and one page in the other.
Queue capability and state use two unsigned bitwise types, one for advertised features and one for dynamic flags, each built from single-bit constants.

Advertised queue features occupy bits 0 through 10 and 12 through 15, covering write cache, forced access, rotation, randomness, statistics, stable writes, synchronous behavior, no-wait, direct access, polling, zoned operation, peer DMA, tagset quiesce skipping, atomic writes and expensive RAID partial stripes. An inherit mask propagates six of them: write cache, forced access, rotation, stable writes, zoned, and expensive partial stripes.
Dynamic queue flags use low bits for write-cache disabled, misalignment, and statistics passthrough.

Queue limits bundle capability and flag words, segment and virtual boundary masks, hardware, device, operational and user sector caps, segment-size and fast-segment caps, physical and logical block sizes, alignment and minimum and optimal IO sizes, discard, secure-erase, zeroing and zone-append caps including unmap variants, discard granularity and alignment, zone write granularity, atomic-write hardware and software maxima, boundaries and unit ranges, segment and integrity and discard segment counts, write-stream count and granularity, open and active zone caps, DMA alignment and pad masks, and an integrity descriptor.
Zone reporting uses a callback that receives a zone descriptor and an index and returns an integer status. A distinct all-zones selector equals the all-ones unsigned value.

Independent access topology pairs single-range records holding directory object, start and length with a container holding its own directory object, registration flag, range count and trailing flexible range array. A request queue object, only partly visible here, links driver data, elevator, multiqueue operations, per-CPU contexts, flags, timeout, depth, references, hardware contexts, usage references, lock tracking, merge hint, queue lock, quiesce depth, disk, queue directory, limits, power, statistics, QoS, identifiers, crypto, timers, shared tags, cgroup state, node, requeue machinery, tracing and flush machinery.

Allocated-vector count is meaningful only to the submitter for append failure and freeing; drivers must not consult it and clones carry no useful value there. The DMA gap hint is valid only after splitting to hardware limits. Bios issued directly to a device lack cgroup queue linkage. New drivers must not set disk address fields because the core allocates them. Zoned topology may change only while no requests are in flight, under queue freeze protection.

Drivers advertising DMA alignment below 511 must tolerate individual vectors whose length is not a sector multiple because offsets can fragment them. At most six cgroup policies are supported per queue. Polling, no-wait and atomic behaviors depend on matching queue features and operation flags; assuming them unconditionally risks blocking or rejection.
